body: Kabuki: Quantum Fighter is Human Entertainment's NES action platformer about an agent entering a threatened computer system. In the overseas story, Scott O'Connor transfers his consciousness into the machine and takes the appearance of a kabuki performer from his ancestry. His long hair becomes a weapon against the hostile creatures encountered inside. The unusual body gives an otherwise technological mission a memorable physical gesture. Attacking means snapping that hair forward, while the surrounding stages turn the infected machine into a dangerous world of platforms and biological-looking hazards.

Scott runs and jumps through side-scrolling stages, using his hair at close range and chip-based weapons against more distant targets. New weapons broaden the choices available as the mission continues toward each boss. The character's movements make the hardware-inspired scenery feel like a place that can be climbed and crossed. The player has to judge where an attack reaches while keeping the next landing in mind. The visual contrast between theatrical appearance and electronic surroundings remains visible in almost every encounter.

The Japanese release, Jigoku Gokurakumaru, was connected to Kaizo Hayashi's film Zipang and used a different protagonist and narrative background. The overseas edition replaced those references with Scott and the computer emergency while retaining the striking fighter. Released in Japan in late 1990, it reached North America the following year. The adaptation demonstrates how much a story could change around an existing set of actions: the performer remains the centre of the screen even when the explanation for his presence changes.
story_headings: A computer mission with a theatrical face
